tickets.title: The catalogue index for 40,000 products and more (**amendment 12, E18, 2026-10-26**)

authority.locator: E18 · section 2 of amendment 12, "Done when" (the owner's requirement of 26 October in section 1 and section 3 decision 1)
authority.requirement: the catalogue's index is sharded (256 content-addressed product shards and 256 id shards by a hash of the product id and of the record id; the manifest names the shards and stays about 55 KB at any size); a product page reads the manifest, one shard and one part; a load reads and rewrites only the shards and parts its products touch; the three collision refusals, the skip, the dry run, the per-product modes, the per-product read, the rollback (bounded by the difference, `rollback_too_large` past 900 checks) and the purge (attachments resolved before a body is deleted, bucket-local, paged, the 15-minute grace) hold across shards; a one-level catalogue is rewritten into shards by its next publication with no operator step; the ingest vocabulary resolves a parted product's ids; verified in the harness at 40,000 products on both hosts and 100,000 on the session host with the real caps; the kits state it.

tickets.outcome: A catalogue of 40,000 products and more is accepted, stored and decided from through a sharded index whose manifest stays about 55 KB at any size: a product page reads the manifest, one shard and one part, and every load, refusal, rollback and purge holds across the shards.

criteria.observable: Capacity (the analyst's SX1): the P86 generator loaded through the import in chunks within the input caps, at N = 40,000 products on both hosts and N = 100,000 on the session host, with the real caps (a part, a product shard and an id shard 2 MiB each): every load answers 200 and no 413 fires; the manifest's bytes are equal within 5% at 5,000, 40,000 and 100,000 products and at most 64 KB plus the shared pieces; every shard object is at most 2 MiB; the per-product read answers the first, a middle and the last product. Today the load is refused 413 manifest_too_large at about 20,300 products (20,250 accepted, 20,312 refused with the generator's ids; the analyst's §0) because the one-level products index rides the one 2 MiB manifest (PUBLICATION_MAX_BYTES, src/config/publication.ts:7) and the id index is one object capped at 8 MiB (ID_INDEX_MAX_BYTES, :713).
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS1 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The page (SX2): on both hosts the anchor's product page reads exactly the head, the set, the four revisions, the anchor's product shard and the anchor's part (8 reads), the same at N = 50, 5,000 and 40,000 products and at 100,000 on the session host; warm (the shard cached per isolate by its digest) it reads no shard and no part; a page with no scoped slot, no anchor, or an anchor whose shard key no shard pointer lists reads no shard; an anchor in a listed shard but absent from it reads that shard and no part; a lost shard or part answers 503 part_unavailable with no fallback. Today the page reads 7 objects and the whole one-level index rides in the manifest (about 2.09 MB cold at 20,250 products; the analyst's §0).
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS2 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The loads and the PUT (SX3): a load reads only the product shards of the products it names and their stored parts, and the id shards only of ids whose place can change (an incoming part record not already in its product's part, an incoming shared piece not already shared, an id a replace, full or move drops), so a retitle reads no id shard; it writes only the shards and parts whose digest moved (an unchanged part is not re-put); the skip on the manifest digest, the dry run (nothing written, shards included) and P91's modes per product behave as today; record_moved (naming both products, and accepted with the source product in the same file), id_in_part and id_shared are refused across shards; the three 413s (index_shard_too_large and id_index_too_large naming the shard and its count, manifest_too_large driven by the shared pieces alone) write nothing; the PUT round trip carries index exactly as read (anything else 422 naming the shard) and removes a product only by an explicit removeProducts list, which also clears a lost part. Today every load reads and rewrites the one id index (src/config/publication.ts:713–735) and re-puts every part it names (src/routes/content.ts:1389), and a PUT removes a product by leaving its pointer out.
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS3 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The migration (SX4): a one-level catalogue built in P86's form (products and idIndex in the manifest) is served by every reader unchanged; its next PUT, import, pull or rollback writes the sharded form with every part digest equal and at most 512 shard writes, with no operator step; a rollback to a one-level revision is written sharded; a tenant whose catalogue declares no productSlots is untouched (LOCK: no shard written and no shard read).
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS4 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The rollback, the purge and the grace (SX5): the rollback's existence check covers every shard the target revision names that the revision in force does not, and every part pointer inside them that differs, refused 410 part_missing naming the missing object, and refused 413 rollback_too_large with the count past 900 checks, nothing written; the purge removes a shard or a part only when no stored revision names it and it was uploaded 15 minutes ago or more, resolves a revision's attachments (its shards, then the parts behind them, bucket-locally, in a paged sweep within its budget) before it deletes that revision's body, and never deletes a body whose attachments are unresolved, shown with the purge's budget exhausted mid-purge. Today the rollback makes one HEAD per product (20,251 at 20,250 products) and the purge deletes a revision body (src/config/publication.ts:1199) before it resolves the parts that body named (:1205–1208), so a budget exhausted between the two loses them for good.
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS5 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The readers (SX6): on both hosts the replay, the receipts, the learn routes, telemetry (still the shopper's own ring only), P85's carousel beacon with its product, the per-product read (manifest, shard, part; 404 for a product no shard indexes, 503 for a lost part) and the ingest vocabulary's product ids each resolve a parted product through its shard; GET /content/catalog answers the sharded manifest and a bounded read of one shard by its two-hex-digit key, never an assembled products list; an event naming a parted product is recognised rather than reported unrecognized (src/reflex/core.ts:934–937); P89 untouched. Today each reader resolves through the manifest's one-level products member (src/content/service.ts:1418, :1547–1549; src/reflex/contentTelemetry.ts:137, :142; src/routes/decisions.ts:791–796) and the vocabulary takes every parted product id from the manifest's keys (src/content/service.ts:488).
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS6 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The kits (SX7): kits 03 and 02 state the sharded index (the manifest's index with its shard pointers, the product shards and the id shards and their keys), the 8-read product page, the caps with their 413 names (index_shard_too_large, id_index_too_large per shard, manifest_too_large driven by the shared pieces alone, rollback_too_large past 900 checks), the removeProducts list, the bounded rollback, that the migration needs nothing from the operator, and the chunking advice (files of about 200–300 products keep a request's storage calls under a few hundred); the one-level sentences are gone: kit 03 :346–348 (one id index of 8 MiB read once per load), :351–353 (a PUT that leaves a pointer out clears a lost part) and :355–358 ("roughly 15,000 to 20,000 products"; "A two-level index ... is not built").
criteria.proof: The P93 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P93.CS7 in src/units/P93/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision, and the reviewer reads the changed sentences at that revision.

criteria.observable: The released artifact shows the behaviour of every LOCAL criterion on both shopper hosts of the acceptance pair at its next release; and a live probe on a pair host measures whether R2 binding calls count toward a per-invocation limit, by loading one file of 250 products and one of 500 products into a sharded catalogue and recording each answer, so the kit's chunking advice (files of about 200–300 products) is confirmed or corrected from the measurement (R-P487, unverified until measured).
criteria.proof: The LIVE1 walkthrough record.

tickets.title: Exact `arm_draw` counts (**amendment 12, E19, 2026-10-26**)

authority.locator: E19 · section 2 of amendment 12, "Done when" (lane L19's finding, R-P485)
authority.requirement: the counter is a durable increment (the learn statistics object or a per-tenant object) so concurrent draws are all counted; the operator's `arm_draw` read is exact; P84 and P85 pass live at the next lane.

tickets.outcome: Every arm-draw outcome the engine counts for the operator is counted, whatever the concurrency, and the learn queue's arm_draw answers that exact count.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a burst of arm-draw outcomes for one tenant recorded concurrently (first requests whose class is capped, mismatched or republished, requests that already carry a session and name a class, which count as ignored, and P85 carousel beacons whose claimed class differs from the engine's, which count as mismatch), issued together without awaiting one another, is counted in full: the learn queue's arm_draw afterwards equals, reason by reason, the outcomes the burst produced. Today recordArmDraw is a KV read-then-write after the answer (src/content/holdout.ts:291–298), so concurrent records overwrite one another and increments are lost (lane L19, R-P485: the ignored answer never counted, one of two mismatches 3 s apart counted).
criteria.proof: The P94 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P94.AD1 in src/units/P94/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The count is a durable increment held by a Durable Object (the learn statistics object, src/durable-objects/LearnStats.ts, at a per-tenant name, or a per-tenant object on an existing binding), never sharing a slot's statistics state, so the operator's read on GET /v1/{tenant}/learn/queue is that object's own count: arm_draw keeps its shape { capped, ignored, mismatch, republished }, its thirty-day window, and names no visitor, session or class; a tenant with no draw reads zeros.
criteria.proof: The P94 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P94.AD2 in src/units/P94/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The count stays off the shopper's time: it is recorded after the answer and never for a synthetic operation (src/routes/decisions.ts:1073–1078; src/content/service.ts:1566); a counter that cannot be written or read neither fails nor delays a decision, a beacon or the learn queue (the queue still answers 200); P84's and P85's unit legs pass unchanged (LOCK).
criteria.proof: The P94 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P94.AD3 in src/units/P94/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Kit 02's learn-queue sentence (docs/kit/02-api-reference.md:1531–1533) states arm_draw as an exact count of every reason over thirty days; "read as a floor" is gone from it.
criteria.proof: The P94 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P94.AD4 in src/units/P94/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision, and the reviewer reads the changed sentences at that revision.

criteria.observable: At the next lane on the pair's next release, P84's and P85's live rows pass on the object host: after a burst of draws, an ignored request and two mismatched beacons seconds apart included, arm_draw on the learn queue equals the draws made, and the P84 and P85 receipts' LIVE1 rows are entered PASS.
criteria.proof: The LIVE1 walkthrough record.

tickets.title: The salt version on long-lived tenants (**amendment 12, E20, 2026-10-26**)

authority.locator: E20 · section 2 of amendment 12, "Done when" (lane L19's finding, R-P485)
authority.requirement: the salt version is derived without walking a bounded history (stored with the rotation, or counted over the whole history), the head script's rotated-paint rule holding on a long-lived tenant.

tickets.outcome: A tenant's salt version is an exact number however long its learn history, so the head script sees every salt rotation on a long-lived tenant as on a new one.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a tenant whose learn history runs past 24 revisions, every revision published with the salt annotation (the salt rotated once inside the first 24 revisions and again after revision 30, unrelated edits between), carries an exact salt version on every learn revision: the number of distinct salts published up to it, one more at each rotation and unchanged by the edits, never null; it is established on the operator's publish without a bounded walk of earlier revisions. Today derivedFor (src/config/publication.ts:251–266) carries the count from the revision before only while that one is within SALT_CARRY_REVISIONS (24, :231) and otherwise walks at most SALT_HISTORY_READS (24) earlier revisions (src/content/holdout.ts:89–121), so from revision 26 on the version is null (lane L19, R-P485: null on the pair's tenant l1).
criteria.proof: The P95 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P95.SV1 in src/units/P95/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: A long-lived tenant whose current learn revision already carries a null salt version because the bounded walk could not reach its first revision (as the pair's l1 does) reads an exact version from its next learn publication on, wherever every one of its learn revisions is still stored; where the stored history cannot establish the count (revisions purged under the retention setting, or a walk that cannot finish) the version stays null, never a smaller number (W21 NR4).
criteria.proof: The P95 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P95.SV2 in src/units/P95/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The head script's rotated-paint rule holds on a long-lived tenant, on both hosts: after a salt rotation past revision 25, the page's context table (GET /v1/{tenant}/context-table/{page}, holdout.saltVersion; src/content/service.ts:1441–1460) and the decision's experiment.saltVersion (:852–853) answer the new exact number, so a browser holding the previous version paints the default row once and draws its class again (src/sdk/head.ts:145–157). Today both read null past the horizon and the head script, which treats null as no rotation, never sees it.
criteria.proof: The P95 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P95.SV3 in src/units/P95/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Locks: the serving path reads no earlier learn revision before the answer (W21 NR3); a count that cannot be established is null, never a smaller number (W21 NR4); a purge never turns an exact salt version into an unknown (W38 B4); experiment.id still names the salt, so the join key is unchanged.
criteria.proof: The P95 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P95.SV4 in src/units/P95/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Kit 02 (:1490–1495 and :1837's purge sentence) and kit 03 (:99, :195) state that the salt version is exact on any learn history the platform still stores and null only where that history cannot establish it; the sentence "The platform reads back at most 24 published learn revisions to count salts; past that horizon `saltVersion` is `null` rather than a smaller number." is gone; kit 01 :642 (the default row painted once after the salt changes) still holds.
criteria.proof: The P95 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P95.SV5 in src/units/P95/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision, and the reviewer reads the changed sentences at that revision.

tickets.title: The new visitor's first answer, decided without waiting on the visitor's record (**amendment 12, E22, 2026-10-26; design R-P547, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E22 · section 2 of amendment 12, "Done when" (E12's definition R-P438; lane L19's timing split); the owner's design direction of 28 October recorded as amendment 13 section 3 row 2 (R-P545) and the design adopted from the root-cause analysis (R-P547)
authority.requirement: the owner decides between overlapping the decision with the session issue, changing how a new shopper's session is issued (P13 D1 reopened), or accepting the deadline's defaults for a new visitor's first view; the chosen design built and measured on the stamps.

tickets.outcome: A new visitor's first answer is decided at once against a blank copy of the brand-new visitor's record and does not wait on creating that record, which is made right after the answer, every safeguard of the first-request door kept, so the first answer's server time on the pair is at most 300 ms.

criteria.observable: The owner's choice, recorded with the owner's words before this ticket's specification: none of (a), (b), (c) as framed; the root cause of the new visitor's record creation found and measured and the first answer redesigned not to wait on it (the record created asynchronously, the profile used after the page is delivered), the safeguards kept by design (R-P545, _evidence/parity-step3/AMENDMENTS.md:1006; amendment 13 section 3 row 2); the design adopted from the root-cause analysis (R-P547, :1008; _evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-first-answer/DESIGN.md).
criteria.proof: Decision D2.

criteria.observable: On both hosts in the harness, a new visitor's first answer at the first-request door is decided by today's own code against a blank in-memory copy of the brand-new visitor's record at the edge, with nothing contacted, created or written before the answer: no Durable Object instance created or fetched (the visitor's or any other), no outbound fetch and no Cache API call (R-P581 F5), and no write to any binding (object storage, the session store, the cache, R2, the queue, D1); its reads are the decision's own (the published content and, on the session host, the session store's two reads of the just-minted session key). With every call to the new visitor's object held H ms (H = 600 in the design's probe), the first answer's total stays below H, as it does with nothing held. The answer is otherwise today's, field by field (decisions, arm, versions, experiment, sources less timings, session and its consent, armRequest) for no class, a class honoured, a mismatch, capped and republished: the door's refusals still come before anything is issued or written (a malformed arm 400, any other 401, touching nothing), the activation's checks still gate the answer (a refusal on the copy answers 401 with no session, no decision, no object and no write), P84's class is minted into the identifier as today, P30's context key is the same on a context-only page, P96's total is on the answer once, and there is no ledger or learning effect (queue 0, ledger objects 0, rings 0). Today the door awaits the activation on the brand-new object (src/routes/decisions.ts:1145–1148 through src/identity/consentContinuity.ts:39–50 and src/durable-objects/ShopperReflex.ts:691–709) and forwards the decision to it (decisions.ts:1156–1158; src/identity/sessionAuthority.ts:746–758): 1 object created, 21 storage calls on the session host and 19 on the do host, 1 write (grantAuthority, ShopperReflex.ts:2358) and 1 output gate before the answer (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-first-answer/DESIGN.md §1, REPRODUCED); live, the session entry is 61–86% of every first answer and the creating trip is 518–1,705 ms longer than the next trip to the same object (37–98 ms; lane L20, records/P96-timings.md).
criteria.proof: The P97 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P97.FV1 in src/units/P97/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, the real record is created right after the answer (outside the answer's time): once the work after the answer is drained, the visitor's object holds exactly grantAuthority for the issued grant and nothing else. A creation lost or not yet made is made by the visitor's next request, whose forward adopts the missing grant (ShopperReflex.ts:554, :3489–3501, :2341–2364): with the creation lost, the next snapshot, action and session route each answer 200 and adopt, nothing else stored; with the next request arriving before the creation, it answers 200, one grant is stored and the creation then completes without changing anything that request or a later one recorded: a consent choice made before the creation lands is still the record's consent after it (the switches it set and its operation kept, the same choice sent again answering 200, the next decision as that choice allows), and on the session host the session's own copy is not restricted by the late creation; a grant already adopted on the record is not activated again (R-P581 F1). Consent is judged switch by switch: a record's newer choice on one switch is kept beside an activation's newer choice on another; and a retried detach (two tabs signing out at once) whose replacement made a newer, more permissive choice in between answers as the first detach did (200), the replacement's own choice kept, while a widening the detach itself would make is still refused (R-P601 N1, N2). A source's newer refusal made after the replacement's choice and carried by the retry is applied (200), its carried choice dated by when it was made, never by the earliest choice's time (R-P605). The session is usable on the next request in every case. Any attempted write by the copy (an effect the write-refusing environment refuses), any change of the copy's record beyond what the activation leaves, and any failure on the copy other than the activation's own refusal (which answers 401 as FV1 says) make the door fall back to today's path, the real activation and forward, with the same minted visitor id and session, and the same answer. Today the record's one lasting write is made before the answer, on the activation (ShopperReflex.ts:696 through :2341–2364), and nothing makes the first answer without it.
criteria.proof: The P97 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P97.FV2 in src/units/P97/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The instrumentation, permanent: the activation's own answer (ShopperReflex.ts:691–709, whichever object runs it) carries an internal X-Owner-Timing header naming its parts, queue, grant, consent, restrict, alarm, commit (storage.sync()) and op, in whole milliseconds; no answer a browser receives carries X-Owner-Timing (the door, the session route, every decision answer); the first-request door's 200 answer carries sources.sessionParts { mint, activate, verify, object } beside sources.timings, its object member read from that header; Server-Timing and sources.timings are unchanged (P76 FA1's names and their add-up, the header's entries equal to sources.timings, P96's one total), and the session route's answer is unchanged. Today the door times only its own session entry around the issue, the activation and the verify (decisions.ts:1145–1148, :1182–1183) and the object reports nothing of its activation (ShopperReflex.ts:691–709).
criteria.proof: The P97 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P97.FV3 in src/units/P97/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.
